key_insight: ParetoSlider is a post-training method for diffusion models that enables continuous, inference-time control over multiple competing rewards by moving along a learned Pareto frontier, avoiding the need for fixed early scalarization.
problem_solved: Addresses the limitation that RL post-training typically collapses multiple objectives into a single fixed weighted reward, preventing users from adjusting trade-offs (e.g., prompt adherence vs. source fidelity) at inference time.
method: Post-train a diffusion model with multiple reward signals instead of a single scalar, preserving multi-objective information.
Introduce a compact, parameterized control (the “slider”) that conditions generation on a continuous trade-off parameter, enabling smooth traversal of the Pareto frontier at inference.
Produce outputs along the learned Pareto frontier so practitioners can pick any point (trade-off) without retraining separate models for each preference.
impact: Enables flexible, interactive trade-off tuning at inference time, reducing the need to train multiple specialized models and improving practical alignment for applications with conflicting objectives.
visual_elements: Pareto frontier plot showing multiple objectives with a highlighted path illustrating continuous movement controlled by a slider.
A horizontal slider UI placed between two example outputs (e.g., high prompt adherence ↔ high source fidelity) demonstrating smooth interpolation.
Before/after side-by-side image edits emphasizing differences as the slider moves (illustrates trade-offs concretely).

paper_title: ParetoSlider: Diffusion Models Post-Training for Continuous Reward Control
paper_authors: Shelly Golan, Michael Finkelson, Ariel Bereslavsky, Yotam Nitzan, Or Patashnik
